source.title: 10 juillet 1940 — les pleins pouvoirs au maréchal Pétain — Assemblée nationale
source.citation_text: French National Assembly records the 10 July 1940 legislative full-powers vote to Philippe Pétain for creating constitutional acts of the État français. The former Republican President of Council had been appointed 16 June and the July 10 authority transfer is not identical to the Constitutional Acts dated 11 July; this is the modeled Vichy regime-start milestone.

source.title: 20 août 1944 — Fin du régime de Vichy — Ministère des Armées, Chemins de mémoire
source.citation_text: French Ministry of Armed Forces memory-history calendar explicitly records the end of the Vichy regime on 20 August 1944. This does not imply all occupied territories had been liberated that day, nor deny the German-controlled Sigmaringen exile succession.

source.title: Ordonnance du 9 août 1944 — Article 7 — Légifrance
source.citation_text: Official French legal text Article 7 identifies the Vichy 'gouvernement de l'Etat français' as an 'autorité de fait'. Article 1 of the same ordinance confirms the French Republic's juridical continuity. Including this as documentary evidence of the de facto authority does NOT legitimize the Vichy constitutional regime.

names.name: Régime de Vichy (État français, autorité de fait)

period.notes: This is only the historically operative de facto Vichy governing regime (État français), recorded as a governing_regime on the stable France COUNTRY UMBRELLA, NOT on the legally continuous stage2:french-republic authority. The French National Assembly records the 10 July 1940 constitutional full-powers vote; the Vichy constitutional acts formalized on 11 July must not be conflated with Pétain's earlier legitimate 16 June Republic appointment. The French armed-forces history calendar dates the regime end at Vichy to 20 August 1944; this is not a day of full liberation of all France nor cessation of any Sigmaringen puppet activity. The official French 9 August 1944 ordinance Art.1 maintains the Republic's legal continuity and Art.7 calls Vichy an autorité de fait; some acts were provisionally preserved by law pending invalidation. The regime was authoritarian and collaborated in discriminatory and persecutory policies. Its context can coincide with CNF/CFLN/GPRF rival authorities on another axis: it claims NEITHER constitutional legitimacy NOR exclusive countrywide territorial control NOR the existence of a separate new sovereign French Polity. No Pétain/Laval Person Activity is fabricated and no populated regional geometry is inferred.
